toegepas.rede_vinder: Blood enters INTO a person; 'by iemand inkom' reads like entering someone's house; same length.
toegepas.fout: 'by 'n ander mens inkom' reads like coming in at someone's place rather than blood getting into a body.
toegepas.rede_keurder: In both versions the blood of a person living with HIV gets into another person; 'in ... inkom' says it plainly and moves nothing.

toegepas.voor: Dit kan by 'n oop wond wees of by 'n naald
toegepas.na: Dit kan deur 'n oop wond gebeur of deur 'n naald
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'by 'n oop wond wees' is vague and wooden; the route is 'deur', and 'gebeur' picks up the previous sentence's 'Dit gebeur'; same length.
toegepas.fout: 'Dit kan by 'n oop wond wees of by 'n naald' is vague and wooden.
toegepas.rede_keurder: In both versions the route is an open wound or a needle that touched blood; 'deur ... gebeur' names it naturally and picks up the previous 'Dit gebeur'.

toegepas.voor: haar praatjie gaan oor bloed en julle sal later
toegepas.na: haar praatjie gaan oor bloed, en ons sal later
toegepas.rede_vinder: In reported speech the narrator's class is 'ons' (as elsewhere in the piece), and AWS needs a comma because both clauses have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: In reported speech by a class member, 'julle' is the nurse's direct-speech pronoun; the narrator's class is 'ons', and two full clauses joined by 'en' lack the AWS comma.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Same people learn later about other routes, the pronoun now fits the reported speech, and the comma follows AWS 2017.

toegepas.voor: Julle kan saam eet en julle kan
toegepas.na: Julle kan saam eet, en julle kan
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Julle kan saam eet' and 'julle kan ... gebruik' are full clauses, so AWS 2017 requires the comma.

toegepas.rede_vinder: Comma closes the relative clause where two verbs meet, so 'nies gee' is not misread.
toegepas.fout: The verbs of the relative clause and the main clause collide ('nies gee'), which makes the reader stumble.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma closes the relative clause where two verbs meet and changes nothing in the meaning.

toegepas.rede_vinder: Comma closes the relative clause where two verbs meet ('byt kan').
toegepas.fout: The verbs collide at 'byt kan', which makes the reader stumble.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma closes the relative clause where two verbs meet and changes nothing in the meaning.

toegepas.voor: Iemand wat met MIV leef kan jou maat of jou onderwyser of jou ouma
toegepas.na: Iemand wat met MIV leef, kan jou maat, jou onderwyser of jou ouma
toegepas.rede_vinder: Comma where the verbs meet ('leef kan'), and a three-item list with one 'of'; the wording 'wat met MIV leef' is kept intact.
toegepas.fout: The verbs collide at 'leef kan' with no comma, which makes the reader stumble on the lesson's key anti-stigma sentence.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma fixes a real stumble, all three people and 'wat met MIV leef' are kept, and the list form beside it is neutral.

toegepas.voor: 'n grootmens te roep en dit is genoeg
toegepas.na: 'n grootmens te roep, en dit is genoeg
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: both clauses have their own subject and verb ('Die eerste ding is', 'dit is'); the safety instruction is unchanged.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two full clauses ('Die eerste ding is ...', 'dit is genoeg').
toegepas.rede_keurder: Punctuation only: the action, who to call and the order are unchanged.

toegepas.voor: As jy tog moet help sit
toegepas.na: As jy tog moet help, sit
toegepas.rede_vinder: Comma after the leading conditional clause where two verbs meet ('help sit'); without it the safety instruction is hard to parse.
toegepas.fout: Without a comma after the leading conditional clause, 'help sit' runs together and the instruction is hard to parse.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Punctuation only: the instruction (put a plastic bag between your hand and the blood) is unchanged and now reads at first glance.

toegepas.rede_vinder: Comma closes the relative clause where two verbs meet ('ken hoef').
toegepas.fout: The verbs collide at 'ken hoef', which makes the reader stumble.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma closes the relative clause where two verbs meet and changes nothing in the meaning.

laat_vaar.voor: van 'n beker of 'n bord of 'n lepel
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: A list of three reads more naturally with a comma and one 'of'; shorter, same meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The repeated 'of' is the story's own rhythm and does not jar for a Grade 4 reader, so this is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: A list of three reads more naturally with a comma and one 'of'; all three items and 'nooit' are kept.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The repeated 'of' in a 'nooit' safety instruction reads well and stresses each item, so the list change is lateral and the wording stays as checked.

na_skrywer.voor: Hulle gaan skool toe en hulle werk en hulle leef
na_skrywer.na: Hulle gaan skool toe en werk, en hulle leef
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: The chain of three 'en hulle' clauses is wooden; sharing the subject in the first half removes one 'hulle', and the AWS comma goes before the clause with its own subject.
na_skrywer.fout: Three full clauses joined by 'en' lack the AWS commas.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The proposal merges the subjects so 'gaan skool toe en werk' suggests the same people go to school and work, or go to work at school, which moves the meaning, so the comma fault needs a different fix.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Jy kan naby haar wees sonder enige gevaar.
vlae.rede: 'haar' refers back to 'Iemand' (maat, onderwyser, ouma) but can be read as Suster Nomsa, and it genders a neutral 'iemand'. 'naby so iemand' would fix it but adds a word to a text at its ceiling, so it is flagged rather than changed.
